title: Non-operational EMP testing at SAMSO and Hill AFB
place_text: San Bernardino; Hill Air Force Base, Utah

tellings.quote: of uh testing that was done uh on our kind of equipment, but it was done at a base like um uh Space Missile Systems Organization in uh San Bernardino Hill Air Force Base in Utah,

related.note: Both are about EMP testing on missile equipment as an explanation for the shutdowns. The WSJ account says an EMP was wheeled up to Malmstrom itself; Salas says such testing was done only at SAMSO and Hill AFB, not at operational bases.

plain: Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down nuclear missiles under his watch, talks about tests of EMP, short for electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics. He says the testing on equipment like his was done not at working missile sites but at places like the Space and Missile Systems Organization in San Bernardino, California, and Hill Air Force Base in Utah, in the 1960s and 70s, drawing on a book called The Faded Giant by James Klotz. He raises it because EMP tests have been offered as an explanation for the missile shutdowns, and the location matters for whether that holds.
